sentences.text:
1  THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE NAMAVARAPU RAJESHWAR RAO  WRIT PETITION No.15912 OF 2025 ORDER:
With the consent of both the parties, this Writ Petition is disposed of at the admission stage itself.
2. Heard Sri CH. Venkat Raman, learned counsel for the petitioner, and learned Government Pleader for Services-I, appearing for the respondents.
3. The case of the petitioner is that she was appointed as a Food Safety Officer in 2020 and has been discharging her duties without any complaints.

On 07.01.2025, respondent No.4 issued a memo based on a news telecast dated 19.12.2024, alleging that the petitioner collected money from traders in Rajanna Sircilla District, and sought an explanation.
The petitioner submitted a detailed reply on 09.01.2025, denying all allegations and clarifying that one Sanjeev, a retired employee, had collected the amount.

After considering the explanation, respondent No.4 issued a Memo vide Ref.No.C2/1355/2024, dated 04.02.2025 stating she should be more careful in discharging her d u t i e s . D e s p i t e t h i s , r e s p o n d e n t N o . 2 i s s u e d a c h a r g e m e m o v i d e Procdgs.Rc.No.3012/E5/IPM/Estt/ 2024-25, dated 04.04.2025, reiterating the same allegations and making additional accusations of misconduct.
On the same day, respondent No.2 also issued a provisional seniority list for the post of Gazetted Food Inspector (Multizone-I), wherein the petitioner was placed at Serial No.3.

However, she was not considered for promotion, while one T.
Sunitha, placed at Serial No.4, was promoted vide Procdgs.Rc.No.5596/E1/IPM/Estt/2025, dated 02.05.2025.
As such, the petitioner submitted a representation dated 08.05.2025, but no action was taken.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner filed the present Writ Petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that appropriate orders be passed in this Writ Petition,
directing the respondents to consider the representation submitted by the petitioner on 08.05.2025 and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.

5. Learned Government Pleader for Services-I, appearing for the respondents, submitted that he has no objection for the disposal of the representation of the petitioner dated 08.05.2025.
6. Taking into consideration the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties,
without going into the merits of the case, this Writ Petition is disposed of, directing the respondent authorities to consider the petitioner's representation dated 08.05.2025, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, as expeditiously as possible, preferably, within a period of six (6)
weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
There shall be no order as to costs.
